name: Inventory turnover
title: Inventory Turnover and DIO: Formula, Periods & Example
description: Understand cost-based inventory turnover, average stock and days inventory outstanding with matched-period examples and interpretation limits.
definition: Inventory turnover measures how many times period cost of goods sold covers average inventory valued at cost. Days inventory outstanding converts that ratio into a holding-period measure using the days in the same reporting period.
explanation: The ratio is based on costs rather than sales revenue. A simple average uses opening and closing stock; seasonal changes can require a more representative prepared average. A high turnover can reflect efficient replenishment or understocking, so it is not an automatic quality score.
formula: Turns = COGS / average inventory. DIO = period days / turns.
formulaNote: Use the same business, cost basis and period. Zero average inventory makes turns undefined; zero COGS does not produce finite DIO.

example.title: Four annual turns imply 91.25 inventory days
example.intro: Use $500,000 annual COGS, $100,000 opening stock and $150,000 closing stock, all valued at cost.
example.answer: Four turns in the 365-day period correspond to 91.25 DIO.
example.assumptions: Same currency, entity and cost scope; a two-point average and 365-day year; no seasonality adjustment.

pitfall.title: Do not mix sales value with cost inventory
pitfall.text: Revenue includes markup. Substituting it for COGS changes the measure; using 365 with quarterly COGS also changes the implied holding time.

tools.text: Calculate matched-period turns, DIO or an entered target average.
Compare a point-in-time current-asset balance with current liabilities.
Review liquidity with inventory excluded from quick assets.

scope: Use one consistent currency and cost-based accounting scope. COGS covers the same period as the average inventory and selected days. The opening/closing mode uses a two-point mean; the known-average mode accepts your prepared average. Targets and 365-day extrapolations are arithmetic scenarios, not industry benchmarks, purchasing instructions or cash-release forecasts.

name: SBA guaranty fee
title: SBA Guaranty Fee: Gross Loan, Guaranteed Portion & FY2027
description: Distinguish an SBA upfront guaranty fee from the full borrower debt, lender annual service fee and usable project proceeds.
definition: The SBA upfront guaranty fee is a program charge on a guaranteed loan that a lender may pass to the borrower under applicable rules. Its calculation depends on the approval-year schedule, loan type, gross amount, maturity and applicable relief; it does not reduce the borrower’s debt.
explanation: For a standard 7(a) loan, the fee schedule uses a gross-approval bracket and the applicable guaranteed portion. That guaranteed portion is lender credit protection, while repayment still covers the full approved gross loan. The lender annual service fee is a different charge and cannot be passed to the borrower.
formula: Supported FY2027 standard example: upfront fee = $250,000 gross × 75% guaranteed × 3% fee = $5,625.
formulaNote: This is a specific example, not a universal fee rate. Manual lender-confirmed fees are required for relief, specialized programs, related 90-day loans and unsupported fiscal years.

example.title: A $250,000 standard approval uses a $187,500 fee base
example.intro: Assume one standard 7(a) approval on November 6, 2026, with a 120-month term and no relief or related loans.
steps: The applicable FY2027 standard upfront fee is 3% of that portion.
Fee = $187,500 × 3% = $5,625; the borrower still repays $250,000 principal.
example.answer: The upfront fee is $5,625 under these specific assumptions.
example.assumptions: Single standard FY2027 7(a) loan; no exception or eligibility inference. A guaranty is not a grant.

pitfall.title: Do not add an already financed fee to gross approval twice
pitfall.text: If the entered gross approval already funds fees, those fees reduce usable project proceeds. Also keep the lender annual service fee out of borrower charges.

tools.text: Estimate supported FY2027 standard or confirmed manual fees and inspect usable proceeds.
Compare general entered loan fees and repayment assumptions.

sources.title: SBA: Terms, guaranteed portions and fee restrictions

scope: U.S. planning estimates in USD. Automatic 7(a) fees cover FY2027 approvals for one standard loan with no fee relief or related 90-day loans. Manual fees handle confirmed quotes without inferring eligibility. All note rates are entered and held constant. The 504 mode uses entered fee amounts and separate amortizing bank/CDC loans; it does not supply a current CDC rate, approval, program-limit certification or refinancing guarantee.
